# /crav1-update-specs-from-changes-and-prs

[All skills](../skills.md) · Walkthrough: [Update specs from changes and pull requests](../../from-update-specs-from-changes-and-prs.md) · Playbook: [`SKILL.md`](../../../.cursor/skills/crav1/crav1-update-specs-from-changes-and-prs/SKILL.md)

## Purpose

Sweep linked repos for changed branches and open or recently closed pull requests, and feed them into the specs.

[`/crav1-update-specs-from-changes-and-prs`](crav1-update-specs-from-changes-and-prs.md) (1.124.0) is one skill with `manual-flow` and `auto-flow`. It runs [`/crav1-add-to-spec`](crav1-add-to-spec.md) for each changed branch and each open or recently closed pull request, including drafts and the host conversation and review threads. It is not a choice on add-to-spec. An optional repo name narrows the run to one `docs/system/repos.md` row.

Default scope is every row with a URL that is not `proposed`, except the specs repo. Manual flow asks once whether to read that repo's pull request comments this time. Auto flow leaves it out unless the repo was named. Neither flow reads the specs repo's branches. Base branches (`main`, `master`, `develop`, `release/*`, and `Merges into`) are not items. Slack, mail, issues, and a new [`/crav1-review-pr`](crav1-review-pr.md) are out.

Manual flow asks once before a read-only fetch, then confirms the inventory (items can be dropped), then goes one by one. Small groups of at most four are offered when there are more than eight items. A spec change is shown before it is written. Auto flow fetches without asking and writes notes and `Synced at` only. Every spec change is a proposal.

State is `docs/system/sweep-progress.md`, written only by `scripts/sweep_progress.py`. A stopped run resumes the same queue and does not redo a finished item. A pull request whose threads were read gets one `Read: sweep` line on its PR note. The budget is 20 minutes unless a number is given, and the script will not go past 45. A failed fetch skips that repo, lists it under Waiting, and the run continues.

The run does not commit, push, post, vote, resolve a thread, or run [`/crav1-review-pr`](crav1-review-pr.md), [`/crav1-pr-status`](crav1-pr-status.md), [`/crav1-resolve-open-questions`](crav1-resolve-open-questions.md), or [`/crav1-finalize-commit`](crav1-finalize-commit.md). Proposals print first in auto flow. Next is this command when items or proposals remain, or [`/crav1-resolve-open-questions`](crav1-resolve-open-questions.md) when a conflict or open question was written onto a spec. The commit stays on Uncommitted.

## Choice words

Exact words for bots and scripted runs (no `--flags`). A word in the invocation takes that choice without asking. A headless or bot run with no word stops and names the valid words.

| Question | Word | Means |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Which flow | `manual-flow` | Ask once before fetching, confirm the inventory, then show each spec change before writing it. An optional repo may follow. |
| Which flow | `auto-flow` | Fetch without asking. Write notes and Synced at only. Spec changes stay proposals. An optional repo may follow. |

The repo is an optional repos.md name, not the characters [repo]. A whole number of minutes may follow. The specs repo stays out unless it is named, or manual-flow is told to read its pull request comments. Its branches are never read.

## Runs when

Many repos or pull requests should be caught up into the specs. Called by the user.

## Prompts

The flow question only when the word is absent, the manual start batch (fetch and, when a specs-repo row exists, its pull request comments), the inventory confirm, and the current item or small group. Auto-flow asks nothing once the word is present. A number of minutes the user left out uses 20 and is outside the budget. Each later item is a later turn. A prompt may hold several questions. See the asking rule in `crav1.mdc`.

## Reads

In short: `docs/system/repos.md`, `Synced at`, sibling checkouts, and open or recently closed pull requests on the host.

Reads `docs/system/repos.md`, `Synced at` lines, the sweep progress file, sibling checkouts, and pull request threads through the same `gh` or `az` reads add-to-spec already uses. It does not read Slack, mail, issues, or production data. It does not log in.

## Writes

In short: `docs/system/sweep-progress.md`, notes and `Synced at` through add-to-spec, a `Read: sweep` line, and spec lines only after a yes.

Writes `docs/system/sweep-progress.md` through `scripts/sweep_progress.py`. Runs [`/crav1-add-to-spec`](crav1-add-to-spec.md) so that skill can write the PR note, its record, and `Synced at`. Writes one `Read: sweep` line on a PR note whose threads were read. Manual flow writes a spec line only after the change is shown and the user says yes. Auto flow does not write spec lines; it records proposals in the progress file.

## Does not

Leaves base branches, the specs repo's branches, a person's `Read` line, and every thread on the host alone. Does not run [`/crav1-review-pr`](crav1-review-pr.md) or [`/crav1-pr-status`](crav1-pr-status.md). Does not commit, push, or delete.

Limits and exceptions: No flow word asks, and a headless run with no word stops. Auto flow cannot record a spec write. A fetch failure skips that repo. The first sweep has no closed-since list. A budget stop finishes the current item and resumes later.

## You run next / Runs by itself

- You run next: [`/crav1-resolve-open-questions`](crav1-resolve-open-questions.md); [`/crav1-update-specs-from-changes-and-prs`](crav1-update-specs-from-changes-and-prs.md); [`/crav1-finalize-commit`](crav1-finalize-commit.md)
- Runs by itself: Runs [`/crav1-add-to-spec`](crav1-add-to-spec.md) for each inventory item, under that skill's note and `Synced at` rules. It does not run [`/crav1-review-pr`](crav1-review-pr.md), [`/crav1-pr-status`](crav1-pr-status.md), [`/crav1-resolve-open-questions`](crav1-resolve-open-questions.md), or [`/crav1-finalize-commit`](crav1-finalize-commit.md).
